c.tagline: A perfectly preserved Ming and Qing old town of purple pottery, ancient wells and China's second-largest Confucius Temple.

taxi.fareNote: Didi is by far the easiest way to book a car; the old town is largely pedestrian, so cars drop you at the gates. Metered street taxis exist but drivers often prefer a negotiated flat rate for trips out to Twin Dragon Bridge or Tuanshan.

emergency.note: 120 is the ambulance number, 119 is fire and 110 is police. English is rarely spoken, so a translation app or your destination written in Chinese helps a lot.

hood_desc: The living heart of old Jianshui (historically called Lin'an), centred on Lin'an Road and the imposing Chaoyang Tower gate, a lattice of stone lanes, courtyard mansions, ancient wells and purple-pottery workshops; the most atmospheric and walkable base, buzzing with local snack stalls after dark.

Modern Jianshui east of the walls, with the railway station, long-distance bus station, chain hotels, supermarkets and everyday services; less charming but the practical, convenient base for transport and cheaper rooms.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as locals do.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:30 AM to 8:30 PM; after that use Didi or a taxi, especially between the old town and the railway station in the new town.
transit.note: Jianshui has no metro; getting around means city buses, Didi, taxis and plenty of walking, as the compact old town is best explored on foot. Buses and Didi link the old town, the new town, the railway station and out to Twin Dragon Bridge and Tuanshan.
transit.pay: Pay city buses in exact-change cash or, more commonly, by scanning with Alipay or WeChat Pay; foreign visitors should set up mobile pay in advance, as it is now the default.

air: Honghe Mengzi Nanhu Airport (nearest, under development)
bus: Intercity coaches to Kunming, Mengzi, Yuanyang and Gejiu
train: Jianshui Railway Station on the Yuxi-Mengzi line (fast trains to Kunming)
Jianshui heritage narrow-gauge tourist railway (Lin'an to Tuanshan)

transit.m: Fast train from Kunming to Jianshui Railway Station (~2.5-3 hr), then a local bus or Didi into the old town
Intercity coach from Kunming South Bus Station to Jianshui (~3-4 hr)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in mainland China and is generally not expected in restaurants, taxis or hotels.

landmarks: Jianshui Confucian Temple (Wenmiao)
One of China's largest Confucian temple complexes, built in 1285, its ceremonial gates, cypress groves and lotus-filled Xuehai pond honor seven centuries of scholarship.
Chaoyang Tower (Chaoyang Gate)
This imposing 1389 Ming-dynasty gate tower, older than Tiananmen and strikingly similar, anchors the old town with swallows wheeling around its triple-eaved roof.
Zhu Family Garden (Zhujia Huayuan)
A labyrinthine Qing-dynasty merchant mansion of 42 courtyards, carved screens and ancestral halls, often called a miniature Forbidden City of southern Yunnan.
Shuanglong Bridge (Twin Dragon Bridge)
A graceful 17-arch stone bridge spanning two rivers since the Qing dynasty, its central pavilion glows golden at sunset over rice paddies and egrets.
Tuanshan Village
A remarkably preserved Qing-era clan village of courtyard mansions, gate towers and carved woodwork, listed by the World Monuments Fund, a short ride west of town.
Jianshui Ancient Town (Lin'an Old Town)
Lantern-lit streets of wooden shopfronts, temples and snack stalls selling grilled tofu, preserving the atmosphere of a 1,200-year-old frontier trading town.
Xuezheng Examination Hall (Qing Imperial Examination Office)
A rare surviving provincial examination compound where Qing-dynasty scholars sweated over imperial civil-service tests, now an evocative museum of China's meritocratic past.
West Gate Ancient Well (Daban Well)
Locals still queue with buckets at this centuries-old sweet-water well, whose rope-grooved stone rim supplies the famous artisan tofu workshops next door.
Jianshui Ancient Town Small Train (Lin'an Station)
A vintage French-era meter-gauge railway experience, trundling in yellow wooden carriages from Lin'an Station past villages to the Twin Dragon Bridge and Tuanshan.
Zitao Street (Purple Pottery Street)
A lively lane of workshops and kilns where artisans hand-throw, carve, and fire Jianshui's famous burnished purple-clay pottery, a craft prized in China for over a century.

train.note: Jianshui has no international trains. From Jianshui Railway Station, trains on the Yuxi-Mengzi line reach Kunming in about 2.5-3 hours and Mengzi in around 40 minutes. Separately, the beloved Jianshui heritage narrow-gauge tourist train trundles from Lin'an Station out through the countryside to Twin Dragon Bridge and the old village of Tuanshan - it is a sightseeing service with fixed departures, booked locally rather than on 12306. Mainline tickets are sold on 12306 with your passport.

bus.note: No international coaches serve Jianshui. Long-distance buses from Jianshui bus station run to Kunming (about 3-4 hours), Mengzi (about 1 hour), Gejiu and the Yuanyang rice-terrace towns, the usual way to continue deeper into southern Yunnan. Tickets are bought at the terminal counter on the day; if you are heading for the Vietnamese border you change at Hekou, which has the nearest crossing.

ferry.note: Jianshui is an inland town on the dry plateau of southern Yunnan and has no passenger ferry services or navigable river.

half.name: Swallow Cavern (Yanzi Dong)
half.blurb: One of Asia's largest karst caves about 30 km east, where swifts nest by the tens of thousands under a vast river-carved arch and climbers scale the walls to harvest their nests each spring.

half.name: Zhijiang & the Ancient Wells
half.blurb: A walking circuit of Jianshui's famous centuries-old wells - Big Well, Little Well and the twin-mouthed wells still used daily - whose sweet water gives the town's tofu and purple pottery their reputation.

full.name: Yuanyang Rice Terraces
full.blurb: The UNESCO-listed Hani rice terraces cascading down the Ailao Mountains, a breathtaking sea of mirrored paddies best at sunrise and sunset, about 2.5-3 hours south of Jianshui.

full.name: Mengzi
full.blurb: The prefecture capital and birthplace of 'crossing-the-bridge' rice noodles, with the elegant Nanhu lake park and colonial-era relics of the old French Yunnan narrow-gauge railway, about an hour away.

full.name: Stone Forest (Shilin)
full.blurb: The surreal grey karst pinnacles of the Stone Forest, a UNESCO site and Yunnan's most famous natural wonder, reachable as a long day trip on the way back toward Kunming.
